## MORRIS IN COURT

A 15-YEAR OLD GIRL'S EVIDENCE

PATHETIC FIGURE.

(Reuter's Service.)

London, October 29.

Three motor cars with blinds drawn arrived at Uckfield Police Court to-day. Several young girls, hooded, emerged and entered the Court, on the occasion of the reappearance of Hayley Morris and his newly-wedded wife before the'magistrates.

A pathetic figure in the witness box was the girl of fifteen who broke down at the previous hearing.

The witness hesitatingly described certain incidents and said Morris told her not to tell anyone and if she wanted money to write to him.

A girl of twenty said that when Morris asked her to go to his room she appealed to Mrs. Morris, who said: "If you like me, you will go, or he will stop my allowance."

Witness said she would go if Mrs. Morris would, and said Mrs. Morris was present during the alleged incident in the room.

## WORLD COAL

STHILH HOILIDING OUR

OWN

EXPERI S. OPINIONS.

(Reuter's Service.)

London, Oct. 20.

Britain's could exports in 1024 were 51.2 per cent. of the world exports, compared with 49.8 in 1913.

Giving evidence to the Coal Commission, Sir Richard Redmayne said he could see no striking change on the world basis, detrimental to British coal interests.

He opined that in a quarter of a century there would be no oil in the United States, and the world supply of oil would suffice more than 80 to 100 years.

## INDIA'S RULER

MR. E. F. L. WOOD THE NEW VICEROY.

(Reuter's Service.)

London, October 29.

It is officially announced that Mr. E. F. L. Wood, the Minister for Agriculture, has been appointed Viceroy of India.

Rt. Hon. Edward Frederick Lindley Wood, P.C. 1922; M. P. (U) Ripon Division, West Riding of Yorks. Born 1881. Major in the Yorkshire Dragoons. Heir to the 2nd Viscount Hallifax. Parliamentary Under-Secretary for the Colonies 1921-2. Author of several publications.

## POLITICS TABOO

MOSCOW'S SUN YAT-SEN UNIVERSITY.

(Reuter's Service.)

The Chinese University named after the late Dr. Sun Yat-sen will be 'opened at Moscow at the beginning of December.

It will accommodate 250 Chinese students.

M. Radek, who has been elected Rector, said the work of the University would be strictly scientific, principally social and would be entirely free from propaganda.

## ALL TO VOTE

## (Router's Service)

Melbourne, October 29.

The Victorian Assembly passed the compulsory Voting Bill imposing a penalty of $2 for failure to vote in State elections.

It is estimated that 250,000 listeners heard the announcement which was broadcast.

## MAJOR DI PINEDO

## FINAL FAREWELLS

TO-MORROW'S DEPARTING

SCENES

CHINESE ELDERS' REQUEST

Final farewell to Hongkong's departing Governor, Sir R. E. Stubbs, K.C.M.G., will be taken to-morrow between 11:15 and 11:30 a.m. at Queen's Pier where representatives of all interests in Hongkong will be present in large numbers. Both interesting and significant of the reciprocation of the feelings of goodwill animating the Hongkong Government and the community with relation to the Chinese notwithstanding the events originating in alien interference is the expressed wish of representative elders of the New Territories to be present at Queen's Pier in order that they may be their presence and good wishes bear testimony to the beneficial results attending the British administration of the New Territories in general and Sir R. E. Stubbs' personal interest and furtherance of their interests in particular. Their presence is entirely at their own request.

There will be five or six of these elders present at the pier to-morrow and they will be introduced to Sir R. E. Stubbs by the Hon. Mr. D. W. Tratman, Secretary for Chinese Affairs.

LEMENTI'S LANDING:

The s.s. "Kalyan" will arrive in Hongkong on Sunday morning and as nearly as can be gauged at the present time Mr. Cecil Clementi will land at Queen's pier at about 9:45. He will be met by Government officials, Unofficial members of the Legislative Council, naval and military representatives and prominent members of the community, will proceed to the Council Chamber where will be administered the oaths and the Constitution read and will then proceed to Government House accompanied by a guard of honour composed of selected men from the East Surrey Regiment. GOVERNOR'S PRIVATE SECRETARY. Mr. T. J. Gaisford-St. Lawrence, Private Secretary to H.E. the Governor, left this morning for Home via Shanghai and America by the "Empress of Canada." It is not known definitely whether Mr. Gaisford-St. Lawrence or Capt. Neville will accompany Sir. R. E. Stubbs to Jamaica.

## REVENUE CASE

WRONGFUL REMOVAL OF TOBACCO.

Before Mr. E. W. Hamilton at the Kowloon Magistracy this morning, Li Wing-chan, of 19, Nathan Road, was charged with removing 595 lbs. of tobacco, 21,625 cigars and 218,400 cigarettes from his bonded warehouse to another part of the premises, and alternatively with keeping the tobacco in an unlicensed warehouse.

Mr. J. A. Fraser, assistant superintendent of Imports and Exports, prosecuted.

Defendant pleaded guilty to the charge of moving the tobacco, which he said was done as the tobacco was deteriorating owing to leaks in the roof.

Mr. Fraser said that since the defendant took the business over from Mr. Atienza two months ago, he had applied for permission to store the tobacco in a shed in the yard. The shed was divided into two by a stone wall, one part being used as a warehouse. On October 22 a revenue officer visited the premises and found that the tobacco had been transferred from the warehouse to the other part used as a bedroom.

A fine of $50 was imposed.

## “HONAM” TRIPS

LANDING "SQUEEZE" STILL HIGH

Conditions similar to those experienced by "Fatshan" passengers on the last trip of that vessel were reported upon the return yesterday from Canton of the s.s. "Honam," those Chinese who could afford to pay the exorbitant suma demanded being able to land and those who could not have to return to Hongkong. The majority found the necessary money.

The s.s. "Fatshan" will return to Canton this afternoon.

## MOTOR ACCIDENTS

TWO PERSONS

INJURED



By a strange circumstance a breakdown van belonging to the Kni Tack Motor Bus Company found itself in a vegetable garden in its endeavour to get to Hunghom yesterday afternoon.

According to the statement of the driver of the van, he turned from Sai Kung Road into Kowloon City Road when the vehicle struck the bank, overturned, and fell into the garden.

The occupants of the van got again before it toppled over.

An inspector of the same Company witnessed another accident at Tsun Wan Road, near Kau Kang village, when a motor truck belonging to the Tai Hing contractors, of Portland Street, Yaumati, struck a bank and overturned.

A Chinese accountant who was riding in the truck was injured and had to be taken to the Kwong Wah Hospital.

According to the eye-witness, the truck swerved in order to avoid a pedestrian, and in so doing steered into the bank.

A motor car owned by a Chinese pulled up near the Naval Yard yesterday afternoon owing to a truck being in the way. A tram car following close behind failed to observe the signal and ran into the motor car, doing some damage to the latter.

At Pokfulam Road, a P.W.D. lorry knocked down a seven-year-old Chinese boy, who was injured in the head and body and had to be taken to the Government Civil Hospital.

## UNMOLESTED

SHAMEEN RESIDENTS AND ANTON



CANTON

ANITARY ARRANGEMENTS

No untoward incidents have taken place since the opening of the postern of the Western (British) gate on Shameen and residents walk generally unmolested and almost unnoticed in the City. Their presence there occasions no comment on the part of passers by and unless they bring parcels back to Shameen they are unmolested. Strike pickets claim the right to examine parcels and to prohibit the carrying into Shameen of foodstuffs.

It was inevitable that in the absence of Chinese workers the sanitary arrangements of the City have had to be left to individuals themselves and conditions as regards the streets and other public places have been of necessity not of the best. Since the arrival of non-Cantonese Chinese scavengers arranged for through the Sanitary authorities at Hongkong, things in this respect have improved considerably.

### “SERIOUS CHARGE.”

## AMERICAN SAILOR'S FIREARMS

An unemployed American seaman named Vertie Vlon Brunson was charged before Mr. S. B. B. McElderry at the Central Magistracy this morning, with unlawful possession of two automatic pistols and 52 rounds of ammunition.

Detective Sergeant O'Donovan said that he visited the Seamen's Institute yesterday evening on certain information received by him and arrested the defendant following the discovery of the arms in his possession.

His Worship told the defendant that it was a serious charge, and remanded the case for one week, bail being allowed on $2,000.

## BLOCKING THE WEST RIVERS

GREATER ACTIVITY.

Whatever the chances of an attack may be, the Reds at Canton are undoubtedly "nervy" with regard to the presence of northern cruisers in the vicinity. The presence of one of them at Hainan taken in conjunction with the fact that Hainan, itself favourable to a resumption of trade and antagonistic to the present Canton administration, have two small gunboats, has led the Reds to greater activity in the matter of laying mines and the patrol of armed launches in the West River. ## TYPHOON WARNINGS

A depression or typhoon of unknown intensity within 120 miles of Lat. 15 N., Long 129 E., which in an earlier warning was stated to be moving W.N.W., is reported this morning to be nearly stationary in Lat. 17 N., Long 128 E. (North-East of the Philippines).

A cyclone or typhoon E. of Luzon, more than 300 miles distant, inclining northward, is also reported this morning.

The forecast for Hongkong for the 24 hours ending at noon tomorrow is N.E. winds, fresh, fine.

### “DISAPPOINTED.”

GERMAN NATIONALS'

PROTEST.

LOCARNO TREATIES.

(Reuter's Service.)

Berlin, October 29.

The executive of the German National party in a manifesto outlining its attitude towards the Locarno treaties says that the pact greatly disappointed the party because of their principles regarding war-guilt and the state of the army. Article sixteen of the League covenant had not been upheld and there had been no reduction in the occupation periods of the Rhineland and Saar as stipulated.

## CANADA'S ELECTIONS

FAVOURABLE CONSER-

VATIVE RETURNS.

(Reuter's Service.)

Ottawa, October 29.

The first returns of the Canadian elections indicate that the tide is flowing in favour of the Conservatives.

## SYRIAN TROUBLE

FOREIGNERS AND DANGER

WARNING NOT GIVEN?

(Router's Service.)

-

Cairo, October 29:

A message from Damascus states that the newspaper "Omran" says that on the 23rd inst. a communiqué from the British Consulate stated that the bombardment was expected to re-start on the 24th in a bit the Consulate would do its best to send British subjects from the danger zone.

Later the same night the French authorities announced that guarantees had been given for payment of the fines imposed on the city, and therefore the danger of bombardment was temporarily over.

The authorities have arrested Hassan el Karrath, who led the band in the insurrection and 43 other insurgents, while 160 Damascenes and suburban residents have been charged with connivance.

The paper adds that three were executed. "We do not know the nature of their crime."

## Washington: Alarmed

Washington, October 29:

Alarmed at the reports from Syria, the State Department has instructed the American Ambassadors at Paris to make representations to the French Government for the protection of American life and property at Damascus.

Later:

According to official reports from Damascus, while the French residents were removed to barricaded positions, the bombardment proceeded without notice to other foreigners.

A demand for indemnification will undoubtedly be made to Paris in respect of damage to American property immediately the details are received.

It is not known what damage has already been done, though hitherto no American has been reported hurt.

Sarrail to be Recalled.

It is reported that one of the first acts of the new Government will be to recall General Sarrail from Syria.

## Earlier Cables

Paris, October 29.

The newspapers are very anxious over the situation in Syria. "L'Echo de Paris" says that M. Doumergue has requested M. Painleve to do what is necessary to re-establish tranquility at any cost. A correspondent of the same paper accuses General Sarrail of pro-Turkish and anti-Arab leanings and of upholding Turkish Freemasonry.

"Figaro" and "Le Matin" criticise General Sarrail's alleged failure to supply information. The latter says that General Sarrail's reports talk about the weather and the dearness of living, with a post-script of two lines in regard to the gravest events.

“Le Matir” declares that General Sarrail's lack of balance is damaging the prestige of France in the world.
